IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p118/r8.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p118/r8.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p118/r8.claim: Some interpret the taunt as reversing the words to mean the addressee is actually base and humiliated.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p118/r8.anchor: فبعض الناس يذهب به هذا المذهب، أي أنت الذليل المهان.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p118/r9.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p118/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p118/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains it as 'noble in your own eyes': Abū Jahl had boasted that no one between Mecca's hills was more powerful or honored.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p118/r9.anchor: وبعضهم يريد: أنت العزيز الكريم عند نفسك. وهو معنى تفسير ابن عباس لأن أبا جهل قال:

BURHAN:v4p58/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p58/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p58/r1.claim: Sarcastic speech says the opposite of what the situation warrants, as in addressing the punished person as noble and honored.
BURHAN:v4p58/r1.anchor: يقرب من هذا التهكم وهو إخراج الكلام على ضد مقتضى الحال كقوله تعالى ﴿ ذق إنك أنت العزيز الكريم ﴾

NAHHAS:v4p134/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p134/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p134/r14.claim: إن is kasra because the clause begins a sentence; the alternative ذق أنك means because you are, but the majority reading in kasra is supported and the boast of being noble is less than the disbelief implied by that alternative.
NAHHAS:v4p134/r14.anchor: كسرت إن لأنها مبتدأ ومن قرأ ( ذق أنك ) جعله بمعنى لأنك وبأنك

RAZI-FULL:v27p215#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p215#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p215#2/r3.claim: One explanation is sarcastic address: the condemned person is called mighty and noble precisely to mean the opposite.
RAZI-FULL:v27p215#2/r3.anchor: أنه يخاطب بذلك على سبيل الاستهزاء ، والمراد إنك أنت بالضد منه

RAZI-FULL:v27p215#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p215#2/r4.speaker: أبو جهل
RAZI-FULL:v27p215#2/r4.claim: Abu Jahl reportedly boasted to the Messenger that no one between the two mountains was more powerful or honored than he, and neither Muhammad nor his Lord could do anything to him.
RAZI-FULL:v27p215#2/r4.anchor: أن أبا جهل قال لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ما بين جبليها أعز ولا أكرم مني

RAZI-FULL:v27p215#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p215#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p215#2/r5.claim: A further explanation is that the person relied on power apart from God and is now told to see what has become of him.
RAZI-FULL:v27p215#2/r5.anchor: أنك كنت تعتز لا بالله فانظر ما وقعت فيه

RAZI-FULL:v27p215#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p215#2/r6.speaker: قارئ أنك
RAZI-FULL:v27p215#2/r6.claim: A variant reads أنك, with the sense “because you are,” rather than إنك.

STUDYQURAN:44:49/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:44:49/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:44:49/r1.claim: One interpretation takes the taunt as God’s direct address to the disbelievers.
STUDYQURAN:44:49/r1.anchor: These verses represent either God’s direct address to the disbelievers

STUDYQURAN:44:49/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:44:49/r2.speaker: IK, Q
STUDYQURAN:44:49/r2.claim: Another interpretation takes the words as spoken by Hell’s guardians to its inhabitants while carrying out God’s command.
STUDYQURAN:44:49/r2.anchor: the words of the guardians of Hell to the inhabitants of Hell while the guardians are carrying out God’s Command (IK, Q)

STUDYQURAN:44:49/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:44:49/r3.speaker: IJ, Ṭ, Z
STUDYQURAN:44:49/r3.claim: The speech ridicules and rebukes the disbelievers for the exalted self-image they held in worldly life.
STUDYQURAN:44:49/r3.anchor: spoken by way of ridicule and rebuke for the exalted image that the disbelievers had of themselves while in this world (IJ, Ṭ, Z)

STUDYQURAN:44:49/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:44:49/r4.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:44:49/r4.claim: Some identify the addressee specifically as Abū Jahl, a Quraysh leader.
STUDYQURAN:44:49/r4.anchor: Some say that these verses refer specifically to Abū Jahl, one of the leaders of the Quraysh

STUDYQURAN:44:49/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:44:49/r5.speaker: Aj, IJ, Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:44:49/r5.claim: Abū Jahl reportedly considered himself mighty and noble among his people.
STUDYQURAN:44:49/r5.anchor: claiming to be mighty and noble among his people (Aj, IJ, Q, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:44:49/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:44:49/r6.speaker: JJ
STUDYQURAN:44:49/r6.claim: “Taste” means to experience the punishment brought upon oneself through disbelief and actions.
STUDYQURAN:44:49/r6.anchor: Taste implies, “Taste the punishment that you have brought upon yourselves through your disbelief and your actions” (JJ; see 3:106

STUDYQURAN:44:49/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:44:49/r7.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:44:49/r7.claim: The reading innaka means “surely you”; some read annaka, “because you are,” linking the doubt to the addressee’s haughtiness.
STUDYQURAN:44:49/r7.anchor: Surely you renders innaka, which is read by some as annaka, meaning, “because you are”(IJ, Q, Ṭ, Z)

STUDYQURAN:44:49/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:44:49/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:44:49/r8.claim: On that reading, their doubt arose from their haughty attitude.
STUDYQURAN:44:49/r8.anchor: they used to doubt because of their attitude of haughtiness

STUDYQURAN:44:49/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:44:49/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:44:49/r11.claim: Here they are mocked for doubting; elsewhere they are chastised for denying the Hereafter’s punishment.
STUDYQURAN:44:49/r11.anchor: While here the disbelievers are mocked for doubting, elsewhere they are chastised for denying the punishment of the Hereafter

BURSEVI:v8p331/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p331/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p331/r1.claim: ذق commands the condemned to taste this humiliating, degrading punishment.

BURSEVI:v8p331/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p331/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p331/r2.claim: Calling him mighty and noble mocks his own estimation and his standing among his people; the intended meaning is the humiliated and abased one.
BURSEVI:v8p331/r2.anchor: في نظرك {الكريم} عند قومك ؛ أي : وقولوا له ذلك استهزاء به ، وتقريعا له على ما كان يزعمه

BURSEVI:v8p331/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p331/r3.speaker: أبو جهل
BURSEVI:v8p331/r3.claim: Abu Jahl boasted to the Prophet that no one between Mecca’s mountains was more powerful or honored, and neither the Prophet nor his Lord could do anything to him; the verse threatens him and his likes.
BURSEVI:v8p331/r3.anchor: روي : أن أبا جهل قال لرسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم : ما بين جبلي مكة أعز وأكرم مني

BURSEVI:v8p331/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p331/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p331/r4.claim: Bursevi calls Abu Jahl’s simultaneous oath by God and denial of divine power an expression of unbelief’s confusion, ignorance, and ego, likening it to demanding stones from heaven.
BURSEVI:v8p331/r4.anchor: عجبا كيف أقيم بالله تعظيما له ، ثم نفى الاستطاعة عنه مع أن الرسول عليه السلام

BURSEVI:v8p331/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p331/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p331/r5.claim: The language of tasting implies that he was already punished in worldly life but, numbed by heedlessness and veiling, felt nothing until death awakened him to the pain of his own injustice.
BURSEVI:v8p331/r5.anchor: وفي لفظ الذوق إشارة إلى أنه كان معذبا في الدنيا ، ولكن لما كان في نوم الغفلة

TABATABAI:44:47-54/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:44:47-54/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:44:47-54/r6.claim: The sinner is addressed while enduring successive punishments.
TABATABAI:44:47-54/r6.anchor: خطاب يخاطب به الأثيم وهو يقاسي العذاب بعد العذاب

TABATABAI:44:47-54/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:44:47-54/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:44:47-54/r7.claim: Calling the sinner mighty and noble while he is abject and vile is mockery that intensifies his punishment.
TABATABAI:44:47-54/r7.anchor: وتوصيفه بالعزة والكرامة على ما هو عليه من الذلة واللأمة استهزاء به تشديدا لعذابه

TABATABAI:44:47-54/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:44:47-54/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:44:47-54/r8.claim: The irony recalls his worldly belief that he had honor and a good outcome with God.
TABATABAI:44:47-54/r8.anchor: وقد كان يرى في الدنيا لنفسه عزة وكرامة لا تفارقانه كما يظهر مما حكى الله سبحانه من قوله

TABATABAI:44:47-54/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:44:47-54/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:44:47-54/r11.claim: The punishment is described as tasting because taste expresses full perception of pains and pleasures.
TABATABAI:44:47-54/r11.anchor: ولذا عبر عن تحمل العذاب بالذوق لما أنه يعبر عن إدراك ألم المولمات ولذة الملذات إدراكا تاما بالذوق

TABRISI:44:41-47/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:44:41-47/r3.speaker: الكسائي
TABRISI:44:41-47/r3.claim: Al-Kisāʾī alone reads the hamzah in “annaka” with fatḥah; the others read it with kasrah.
TABRISI:44:41-47/r3.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي وحده ذق أنك بفتح الهمزة والباقون إنك بكسرها

TABRISI:44:47-50/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:44:47-50/r5.speaker: مقاتل
TABRISI:44:47-50/r5.claim: Muqātil says the fire's keeper takes the sinner over the fire; his head comes apart from his brain, and the boiling liquid is poured into it.
TABRISI:44:47-50/r5.anchor: قال مقاتل: إن خازن النار يمر به على رأسه

TABRISI:44:47-50/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:44:47-50/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:44:47-50/r6.claim: Al-ḥamīm here is water whose heat has reached its extreme.
TABRISI:44:47-50/r6.anchor: وهو الماء الذي قد انتهى حره

TABRISI:44:47-50/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:44:47-50/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:44:47-50/r7.claim: The angel taunts him for his former boast that he was the mightiest and most honored person in the valley, calling him self-exalting in his own claim.
TABRISI:44:47-50/r7.anchor: وذلك أنه كان يقول أنا أعز أهل الوادي وأكرمهم

TABRISI:44:47-50/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:44:47-50/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:44:47-50/r8.claim: One explanation treats the wording as the opposite of its surface sense: he is actually abject and humiliated, while the stated praise mocks him.
TABRISI:44:47-50/r8.anchor: وقيل: إنه على معنى النقيض فكأنه قيل إنك أنت الذليل المهين إلا أنه قيل على هذا الوجه للاستخفاف به

TABRISI:44:47-50/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:44:47-50/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:44:47-50/r9.claim: Another explanation takes him as genuinely honored among his people, but says that status did him no good.
TABRISI:44:47-50/r9.anchor: وقيل: معناه إنك أنت العزيز في قومك الكريم عليهم فما أغنى ذلك عنك

THALABI:v8p355#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p355#2/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p355#2/r6.claim: The taunt is directed at Abu Jahl, who claimed nobody between the two ends of Mecca was more powerful or noble than he.
THALABI:v8p355#2/r6.anchor: إنك أنت العزيز في قومك. الكريم بزعمك، وذلك إن أبا جهل.

THALABI:v8p355#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p355#2/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p355#2/r7.claim: The keepers address him with this phrase in derision and as a pointed affirmation of what he had claimed.
THALABI:v8p355#2/r7.anchor: فيقول له الخزنة هذا على طريق الاستخفاف والتحقيق

THALABI:v8p355#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p355#2/r8.speaker: الكسائي
THALABI:v8p355#2/r8.claim: The common reading begins a new sentence with inna in the genitive; al-Kisai reads it in the accusative, meaning because you are.
THALABI:v8p355#2/r8.anchor: وقراءة العامة إنك بكسر الألف على الابتداء، وقرأ الكسائي بالنصب على معنى لأنك.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p120/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p120/r3.speaker: عكرمة والكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p120/r3.claim: Ikrima and al-Kalbi report that Muhammad warned Abu Jahl to expect God's punishment; Abu Jahl boasted that neither Muhammad nor God could harm him, and after his death at Badr this verse recalled and humiliated him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p120/r3.anchor: قال عكرمة والكلبي: التقى النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- وأبو جهل فقال له النبي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p120/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p120/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p120/r4.claim: The exegetes say the angel taunts Abu Jahl by repeating his boast that he was the most powerful and honored man in the valley.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p120/r4.anchor: وهذا قول أهل التفسير قالوا: إنه كان يقول أنا أعز أهل الوادي وأكرمهم، فيقول له الملك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p120/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p120/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p120/r5.claim: Abu Ishaq paraphrases the command as taste this punishment, since you claimed to be the mighty and honored one.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p120/r5.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: المعنى: ذق هذا العذاب، إنك أنت القائل: أنا العزيز الكريم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p120/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p120/r6.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p120/r6.claim: Abu Ali says the description is true only according to Abu Jahl's own claim, as with the question about alleged partners in 28:62.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p120/r6.anchor: وقال أبو علي الفارسي: المعنى: إنك أنت العزيز الكريم في زعمك وفيما تقوله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p120/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p120/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p120/r7.claim: Abu Ali's reading is illustrated by the poet called Zahra al-Yaman boasting that he is the mighty one, and Jarir's retort to him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p120/r7.anchor: أن زهرة اليمن (¬2) قال في جرير: أبلغ كليبا وأبلغ عنك شاعرها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p120/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p120/r8.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p120/r8.claim: The wording is ironic rebuke, like the unbelievers' mocking address to Muhammad in 15:6: the text throws Abu Jahl's own boast back at him, though it is untrue.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p120/r8.anchor: نحو هذا قال صاحب النظم قال: هذا على وجه المعارضة والتبكيت

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:44:42-51/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:44:42-51/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:44:42-51/r6.claim: The taunt echoes Abu Jahl's own boast that nobody between the two mountains was more powerful or generous than he was.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:44:42-51/r6.anchor: وذلك أنه قال: ما بين جبليها أعز ولا أكرم مني

QASHANI:44:49-54/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:44:49-54/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:44:49-54/r1.claim: This taunt signals reversed conditions caused by a corrupted primordial nature: bodily pleasure, might, and psychic dignity become spiritual pain, humiliation, and abasement.
QASHANI:44:49-54/r1.anchor: إشارة إلى انعكاس أحوالها لانتكاس فطرتها

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:44:40/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:44:40/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:44:40/r4.claim: The taunt that the condemned is mighty and noble ironically exposes the helplessness of people who trusted their worldly power and thought themselves untouchable.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:44:40/r4.anchor: dünyada güçlerine güvenen, kendilerini değerli ve önemli bilen

BURHAN:v2p320/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p320/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p320/r6.claim: “Taste! You are the mighty, noble one” is an example of denial and rebuke.
BURHAN:v2p320/r6.anchor: ومنها الانكار والتبكيت نحو ﴿ ذق إنك أنت العزيز الكريم ﴾ 4

BURHAN:v2p216/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p216/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p216/r3.claim: Another mode is specific address intended for its specific addressee, illustrated by the rebuke, threat, command to the Messenger, and Zayd’s divorce.
BURHAN:v2p216/r3.anchor: الثاني خطاب الخاص والمراد به الخصوص

BURHAN:v2p229/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p229/r10.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p229/r10.claim: The address to Abu Jahl is taḥakkum, a taunting reversal of his boast that no one between Mecca’s mountains was more mighty or noble than he.
BURHAN:v2p229/r10.anchor: وهو خطاب لآبي جهل لأنه قال ما بين جبليها يعني مكة أعز ولا اكرم مني

BURHAN:v4p54/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p54/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p54/r3.claim: The command to taste and the praise as mighty and noble are phrased according to the addressee's own presumed belief.
BURHAN:v4p54/r3.anchor: وقوله ﴿ ذق إنك أنت العزيز الكريم ﴾ 3

BURHAN:v2p200/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p200/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p200/r1.claim: Context can resolve ambiguity, rule out unintended readings, specify general wording, and restrict unqualified wording; ignoring it leads to error. Thus the address 'the mighty, noble one' in context means the truly lowly and contemptible.
BURHAN:v2p200/r1.anchor: الرابع دلالة السياق فإنها ترشد إلى تبيين المجمل والقطع بعدم احتمال غير المراد وتخصيص العام وتقييد المطلق

BURHAN:v2p313/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p313/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p313/r4.claim: The verse is reported to have been revealed about Abu Jahl, who claimed that no one between Mecca's two hills was more powerful or noble than he.
BURHAN:v2p313/r4.anchor: نزلت في أبي جهل لانه قال ما بين أخشبيها أي جبليها يعني مكة اعز مني ولا اكرم

BURHAN:v2p313/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p313/r5.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v2p313/r5.claim: Another explanation is that the address is spoken sarcastically.

ITQAN:v3p218#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p218#2/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p218#2/r3.claim: Imperatives may function as a lower person’s prayer, a threat, an insult, humiliation through transformation (narrower than insult), or a challenge exposing inability.
ITQAN:v3p218#2/r3.anchor: والإهانة نحو ﴿ ذق إنك أنت العزيز الكريم ﴾

ITQAN:v3p124/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p124/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p124/r4.claim: An oppositional metaphor joins meanings that cannot coexist; its taunting subtypes use a word for its opposite, as in ‘glad tidings’ for warning, ironic praise of Shuʿayb’s opponents, and ‘the mighty, noble’ for humiliation.
ITQAN:v3p124/r4.anchor: ومن العنادية التهكمية والتمليحية وهما ما استعمل في ضد أو نقيض

ITQAN:v3p89/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p89/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p89/r6.claim: A twelfth form is sarcastic address, exemplified by the taunt “Taste; you are the mighty, noble one.”
ITQAN:v3p89/r6.anchor: الثاني عشر خطاب التهكم نحو ﴿ ذق إنك أنت العزيز الكريم ﴾

DAMGHANI:v1p322/r7.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p322/r7.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p322/r7.claim: Al-ʿazīz can mean impregnable or mighty; Dāmghānī applies this sense to the taunt in 44:49 and parallel descriptions of strength.
DAMGHANI:v1p322/r7.anchor: في سورة الدخان ذق انك انت العزيز الكريم نزلت في ابي جهل

DAMGHANI:v1p322/r8.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p322/r8.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p322/r8.claim: Dāmghānī says the taunt calling the condemned man mighty and noble was revealed concerning Abū Jahl.
DAMGHANI:v1p322/r8.anchor: ذق انك انت العزيز الكريم نزلت في ابي جهل

DAMGHANI:v1p403/r1.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p403/r1.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p403/r1.claim: In the taunt ‘the mighty, noble one,’ karīm is a self-description in the condemned person’s own claim.
DAMGHANI:v1p403/r1.anchor: الكريم في زعمه ( أي زعم نفسه ) قوله تعالى في سورة الدخان

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p521/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p521/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p521/r6.claim: A fifth sense is arrogant or self-important, used mockingly in “the mighty, noble one.”
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p521/r6.anchor: والخامس : المتكبر . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة الدخان

MAJAZ:v2p209/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p209/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p209/r2.claim: The taunting titles call the condemned man what he was in worldly life.
MAJAZ:v2p209/r2.anchor: «ذق إنك أنت العزيز الكريم» (49) فى الدنيا..

SAMIN-DURR:44:49/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:44:49/r1.speaker: الكسائي
SAMIN-DURR:44:49/r1.claim: Al-Kisaʾi reads إنك with fatḥ, causally meaning because you; the others use kasra as an independent clause that also conveys a reason, so the readings converge in meaning.
SAMIN-DURR:44:49/r1.anchor: قرأه الكسائي بالفتح على معنى العلة أي: لأنك. وقيل: تقديره: ذق عذاب أنك أنت

SAMIN-DURR:44:49/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:44:49/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:44:49/r2.claim: The address is sarcastic, intensifying the humiliation; Jarir uses the same taunt against a poet who called himself زهرة اليمن.
SAMIN-DURR:44:49/r2.anchor: وهذا الكلام على سبيل التهكم، وهو أغيظ للمستهزأ به، ومثله قول جرير لشاعر سمى نفسه زهرة اليمن:

ZAJJAJ:v4p428/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p428/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p428/r4.claim: All readers except al-Kisaʾi read inna with kasra; al-Kisaʾi reads anna with fatḥa.
ZAJJAJ:v4p428/r4.anchor: الناس كلهم على كسر " إنك " إلا الكسائي وحده فإنه قرأ: ذق أنك

ZAJJAJ:v4p428/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p428/r5.speaker: الكسائي
ZAJJAJ:v4p428/r5.claim: On al-Kisaʾi's reading, the condemned man is told to taste punishment because he had boasted that he was the mightiest and most protected man in the valley.
ZAJJAJ:v4p428/r5.anchor: إلا الكسائي وحده فإنه قرأ: ذق أنك أنت، أي لأنك قلت

ASAD-NOTES:44:43#n27/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:44:43#n27/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:44:43#n27/r1.claim: The taunt addresses the arrogance of disbelief in life after death and, consequently, in humanity's ultimate accountability to God.
ASAD-NOTES:44:43#n27/r1.anchor: thus alluding to the sin of arrogance due to disbelief in a continuation of life after death and, hence, in man's ultimate responsibility to God.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p11/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p11/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p11/r1.claim: Although glad tidings normally announce something good, telling hypocrites of punishment and calling the condemned man mighty and noble are sarcastic mockery.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p11/r1.anchor: المعروف أن التبشير بالشيء الحسن أما هنا فجاء التبشير من باب السخرية والتهكم منهم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p876/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p876/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p876/r3.claim: Context is a major clue to meaning: “Taste, you are the mighty, noble one” sounds like praise alone, but in context it is condemnation.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p876/r3.anchor: إذا أخذت من سياقها تظهر وكأنها مدحا بينما في الواقع هي في معرض الذم

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p220/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p220/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p220/r2.claim: The passage presents intellectual and historical evidence for reward and punishment, then depicts the fates of believers and disbelievers; God treats them differently with complete justice.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p220/r2.anchor: logical as well as historical arguments in favour of reward and punishment are briefly referred to. It is mentioned in detail that God will not deal equally between those who spent their lives

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p239/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p239/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p239/r3.claim: The coming section identifies disbelief in life after death as the cause of Quraysh rebellion and heedlessness of the future.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p239/r3.anchor: the real reason for the rebelliousness of the Quraysh is highlighted: they do not imagine that there is life after this worldly existence

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p239/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p239/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p239/r4.claim: The section first offers intellectual and natural arguments for reward and punishment, then describes the fate of believers and disbelievers.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p239/r4.anchor: first the intellectual and natural arguments which substantiate the law of reward and punishment are cited. After this, the fate of both the believers and the disbelievers is depicted.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p243/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p243/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p243/r6.claim: The taunt can be read as an expression of the punishment and situation that now befall the sinner, rather than as speech by an identified speaker.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p243/r6.anchor: This statement can be an expression of the situation that will befall these people

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p243/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p243/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p243/r7.claim: Alternatively, the taunt may be spoken by Hell’s wardens.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p243/r7.anchor: it can also be interpreted to be made by the wardens.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p243/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p243/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p243/r8.claim: The sinners who once posed as powerful and honourable, arrogantly denied the Day, and doubted it are told to taste the very torment they questioned.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p243/r8.anchor: they posed to be very powerful and honourable in the previous world

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p166#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p166#2/r1.speaker: الكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p166#2/r1.claim: Al-Kisai alone opens the hamza in أنك; all the other readers kasra it.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p166#2/r1.anchor: قال: قرأ الكسائي وحده: ذق أنك أنت العزيز الكريم [الدخان/ 49]. وقرأ الباقون: إنك بكسر الألف .

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p166#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p166#2/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p166#2/r2.claim: With kasra, the taunt echoes the condemned man's own boast and Abu Jahl's claim; a reported poem and Jarir's reply illustrate the boast.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p166#2/r2.anchor: من كسر أن* فعلى ما كان يقوله، فالمعنى: إنك أنت العزيز الكريم في زعمك

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p166#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p166#2/r3.speaker: بعض الرواة
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p166#2/r3.claim: A reported poem has Zahrat al-Yaman call himself the illustrious one, and Jarir answers by reminding him of his prior boasting.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p166#2/r3.anchor: وأخبرنا بعض الرواة أن زهرة اليمن قال في جرير: أبلغ كليبا وأبلغ عنك شاعرها أني الأغر

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p166#2/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p166#2/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p166#2/r4.claim: The source also cites Abu Jahl's boast that he was the mightiest and most protective man in the valley.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p166#2/r4.anchor: وكذلك أبو جهل كان يقول: أنا أعز الوادي وأمنعهم، فعلى ما يقول جاء التنزيل بتكذيبه

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p166#2/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p166#2/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p166#2/r5.claim: With the fatḥa reading, ذق أنك means ذق بأنك, taste because you are so.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p166#2/r5.anchor: فأما قول الكسائي: ذق أنك بفتح الهمزة فالمعنى: ذق بأنك

NASHR:v2p371/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p371/r4.speaker: الكسائي
NASHR:v2p371/r4.claim: Al-Kisaʾi opens the hamza in إنك; the other readers kasra it.
NASHR:v2p371/r4.anchor: فقرأ الكسائي بفتح الهمزة، وقرأ الباقون بكسرها

QIRAAT-ER:44:49:2#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:44:49:2#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:44:49:2#1/r1.claim: The vowel variant changes inna-ka to anna-ka, permitting a more subordinating or object-like clause link.
QIRAAT-ER:44:49:2#1/r1.anchor: Canonical vowel variant changes إِنَّكَ (innaka) to أَنَّكَ (annaka), allowing a more subordinating

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p209/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p209/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p209/r1.claim: Qatāda says the threat was revealed about Abū Jahl, who boasted that no one between Mecca's two mountains was more powerful or noble; God answers him ironically, “Taste, you are the mighty, noble one.”
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p209/r1.anchor: عن قتادة قال لما نزلت في أبي جهل ﴿ خذوه فاعتلوه إلى سواء الجحيم ﴾ قال قتادة قال أبو جهل

ALUSI-FULL:v25p134#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p134#2/r1.speaker: عكرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v25p134#2/r1.claim: Ikrima reports that Abu Jahl boasted to the Prophet that neither he nor his companion could harm him, since he protected the people of the valley and was noble; after Badr, God humiliated him with this taunt.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p134#2/r1.anchor: عن عكرمة أن أبا جهل قال للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ما تستطيع لي أنت ولاصاحبك من شيء

ALUSI-FULL:v25p134#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p134#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p134#2/r2.claim: Another report says Abu Jahl asked Quraysh to guess his name, rejected Umar, al-Jallas, and Abu al-Hakam, then called himself al-Aziz al-Karim; the verses about the tree of Zaqqūm then came down.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p134#2/r2.anchor: وروي أن اللعين قال يوما : يا معشر قريش أخبروني ما اسمي فذكرت له ثلاثة أسماء عمر

ALUSI-FULL:v25p134#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p134#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p134#2/r3.claim: The verse is not restricted to Abu Jahl: every sinner who makes a similar claim will be addressed this way at the Resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p134#2/r3.anchor: وهذا ونحوه لا يد لأيضاع لى تخصيص حكم الآية به فكل أثيم يدعى دعواه كذلك يوم القيامة

ALUSI-FULL:v25p134#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p134#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p134#2/r4.claim: Another explanation is: taste this, though you were mighty among your people and honored by them; that status did not benefit you. Tasting is a metaphor for experiencing.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p134#2/r4.anchor: وقيل : المعنى ذق إنك العزيز في قومك الكريم عليهم فما أغنى ذلك عنك ولم يفدك شيئا

ALUSI-FULL:v25p134#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p134#2/r5.speaker: الحسن بن علي بن أبي طالب والكسائي
ALUSI-FULL:v25p134#2/r5.claim: Al-Hasan ibn Ali and al-Kisaʾi read anna with fatḥa on the hamza, understood as because you are.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p134#2/r5.anchor: وقرأالحسنبن علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله تعالى عنهما على المنبرو الكسائي ( أنك ) بفتح الهمزة على معنى لأنك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p236#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p236#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p236#2/r6.claim: The condemned is told to taste the punishment.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p236#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p236#2/r7.speaker: الكسائي والآخرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p236#2/r7.claim: Al-Kisāʾī opens the hamza in annaka, meaning 'because you used to say I am mighty'; the others use kasra and begin a new clause.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p236#2/r7.anchor: قرأ الكسائي "أنك" بفتح الألف، أي لأنك كنت تقول

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p236#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p236#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p236#2/r8.claim: The title 'mighty and noble' is attributed to him only by his people and according to his own claim; the keepers say it in contempt and rebuke.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p236#2/r8.anchor: عند قومك بزعمك، وذلك أن أبا جهل كان يقول

BAYDAWI-FULL:44:48-52/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:44:48-52/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:44:48-52/r2.claim: The guardians say this mockingly to taunt him with the claim to honor and might he used to make.
BAYDAWI-FULL:44:48-52/r2.anchor: أي وقولوا له ذلك استهزاء به وتفريعا على ما كان يزعمه

BAYDAWI-FULL:44:48-52/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:44:48-52/r3.speaker: الكسائي
BAYDAWI-FULL:44:48-52/r3.claim: Al-Kisāʾī reads anna with fatḥ, construing it as taste because you are or connecting it with an omitted punishment.
BAYDAWI-FULL:44:48-52/r3.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي «أنك» بالفتح أي ذق لأنك أو { عذاب }

BIQAI-FULL:v7p82/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p82/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p82/r1.claim: The taunting command recalls the messengers' worldly warning that the sinner was lowly, which he and his followers denied; repeating their boast adds rebuke and torment.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p82/r1.anchor: حكى له قولهم على ما كانوا يلفظون به زيادة في تذعيبه بالتوبيخ والتقريع معللا للأمر بالذوق

BIQAI-FULL:v7p82/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p82/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p82/r2.claim: أنت is emphatic and isolates him as the one supposedly mighty, in contrast to those who truthfully exposed his worthlessness.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p82/r2.anchor: وأكد بقوله : { أنت } وحدك دون هؤلاء الذين يخبرون بحقارتك

BIQAI-FULL:v7p82/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p82/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p82/r3.claim: العزيز means one who overcomes and is never overcome; الكريم combines generosity with dignity of soul and proud refusal.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p82/r3.anchor: العزيز } أي الذي يغلب ولا يغلب { الكريم } أي الجامع إلى الجود شرف النفس وعظم الإباء

BIQAI-FULL:v7p82/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p82/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p82/r4.claim: The apparent praise is an ironic accusation of baseness, established by the sinner's present ruin rather than concealed by pretended high character.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p82/r4.anchor: فهو كناية عن مخاطبته بالخسة مع إقامة الدليل على ذلك بما هو فيه من المهالك

BIQAI-FULL:v7p82/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p82/r5.speaker: الكسائي
BIQAI-FULL:v7p82/r5.claim: Al-Kisa'i reads إن with fatḥ, making the punishment both spoken and enacted in the same way the sinner was praised in worldly life and believed himself deserving of praise.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p82/r5.anchor: وقراءة الكسائي بفتح ( إن ) دالة على هذا العذاب قولا وفعلا

DURR-FULL:v7p419/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p419/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v7p419/r1.claim: The taunt recalls Abu Jahl's boast of being mighty and noble; God killed and humiliated him at Badr, turning his own words against him.
DURR-FULL:v7p419/r1.anchor: وأنا العزيز الكريم فقتله الله يوم بدر وأذله وعيره بكلمته {ذق إنك أنت العزيز الكريم}

DURR-FULL:v7p419/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p419/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p419/r2.claim: Qatāda reports Abu Jahl asking how Muhammad could threaten him when he was the mightiest man between the two mountains; the verse was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v7p419/r2.anchor: عن قتادة قال: قال أبو جهل: أيوعدني محمد وأنا أعز من مشى بين جبليها فنزلت

DURR-FULL:v7p419/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p419/r3.claim: An unnamed report says Abu Jahl declared his name to be “the mighty, the noble”; the verses about the Zaqqum tree then descended.
DURR-FULL:v7p419/r3.anchor: عن [] قال: أخبرت أن أبا جهل قال: يا معشر قريش أخبروني ما اسمي

DURR-FULL:v7p419/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p419/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p419/r4.claim: After the order to drag him into Hell, Abu Jahl claimed no man between the mountains was mightier or nobler, and God answered with this taunt.
DURR-FULL:v7p419/r4.anchor: عن قتادة قال لما نزلت {خذوه فاعتلوه إلى سواء الجحيم} قال أبو جهل: ما بين جبليها رجل أعز ولا أكرم مني

DURR-FULL:v7p419/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p419/r11.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v7p419/r11.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the address is sarcastic: Abu Jahl is humiliated then, although he had treated himself as mighty and noble without God's honor and might.
DURR-FULL:v7p419/r11.anchor: عن ابن جريج في قوله: {ذق إنك أنت العزيز الكريم} قال: هو يومئذ ذليل ولكنه يستهزأ به

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3290/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3290/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3290/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the taunt as meaning that the punished person is neither mighty nor noble.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3290/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : ذق انك انت العزيز الكريم يقول : لست بعزيز ولا كريم .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p315/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p315/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p315/r5.claim: ذق إنك أنت العزيز الكريم is a separate quoted utterance, with an omitted verb such as 'say to him' or 'it is said to him.'
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p315/r5.anchor: وجملة { ذق إنك أنت العزيز الكريم } مقول قول آخر محذوف تقديره : قولوا له أو يقال له .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p315/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p315/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p315/r6.claim: Taste is metaphorical for experiencing, and the imperative is used to humiliate.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p315/r6.anchor: والذوق مستعار للإحساس وصيغة الأمر مستعملة في الإهانة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p316/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p316/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p316/r1.claim: The statement 'you are the mighty, noble one' is sarcastic by antithesis and means the opposite, that he is abased and humiliated; emphasis heightens the sarcasm.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p316/r1.anchor: وقوله : { إنك أنت العزيز الكريم } خبر مستعمل في التهكم بعلاقة الضدية . والمقصود عكس مدلوله ، أي أنت الذليل المهان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p316/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p316/r2.speaker: الكسائي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p316/r2.claim: Most readers have kasra on إنك; al-Kisāʾī reads it with fatḥa, construed with an implied lām of purpose.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p316/r2.anchor: وقرأه الجمهور بكسر همزة { إنك } . وقرأه الكسائي بفتحها على تقدير لام التعليل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p316/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p316/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p316/r3.claim: The detached nominative أنت emphasizes the attached pronoun in إنك; an attached object pronoun is emphasized only by a detached nominative pronoun.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p316/r3.anchor: وضمير المخاطب المنفصل في قوله : { أنت } تأكيد للضمير المتصل في { إنك } ولا يؤكد ضمير النصب المتصل إلا بضمير رفع منفصل .

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p350#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p350#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p350#3/r1.claim: An angel tells him to taste the punishment.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p350#3/r1.anchor: ثم يقول له الملك ذق العذاب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p350#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p350#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p350#3/r2.claim: Calling him mighty and noble is a taunt; Abu Jahl used to claim he was Quraysh's most powerful and honored man.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p350#3/r2.anchor: هذا توبيخ له بذلك وكان أبو جهل يقول أنا أعز قريش وأكرمها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p350#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p350#3/r3.speaker: الكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p350#3/r3.claim: Al-Kisaʾi reads the hamza in anna with fatḥa; the other readers use kasra.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p350#3/r3.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي ذق أنك بفتح الهمزة والباقون بكسرها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p350#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p350#3/r4.speaker: أبو علي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p350#3/r4.claim: Abu ʿAli explains kasra as “you are mighty according to your own claim,” and fatḥa as “because you are.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p350#3/r4.anchor: قال أبو علي من كسرها فالمعنى أنت العزيز في زعمك ومن فتح فالمعنى بأنك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p350#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p350#3/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير ومقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p350#3/r5.claim: One answer to the question why he is called mighty though he is not is that the words mock him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p350#3/r5.anchor: أحدها أنه قيل ذلك استهزاء به قاله سعيد بن جبير ومقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p350#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p350#3/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p350#3/r6.claim: Qatada says he is mighty and noble only in his own estimation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p350#3/r6.anchor: والثاني أنت العزيز الكريم عند نفسك قاله قتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p350#3/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p350#3/r7.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p350#3/r7.claim: Al-Mawardi says he was powerful among his people and honored by his family.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p350#3/r7.anchor: والثالث أنت العزيز في قومك الكريم على أهلك حكاه الماوردي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p260/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p260/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p260/r8.claim: The address calling the condemned “mighty and noble” is spoken sarcastically to mock and rebuke him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p260/r8.anchor: قولوا له ذلك على وجه التهكم والتوبيخ

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p260/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p260/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p260/r9.claim: Al-Dahhak reports Ibn Abbas’s gloss: the condemned is neither mighty nor noble.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p260/r9.anchor: وقال الضحاك عن ابن عباس: أي لست بعزيز ولا كريم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p260/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p260/r10.speaker: عكرمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p260/r10.claim: Ikrimah recounts that Abu Jahl boasted to the Prophet that neither the Prophet nor his Lord could overcome him and called himself mighty and noble; after God killed and humiliated him at Badr, this verse taunted him with his own words.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p260/r10.anchor: عن عكرمة قال: لقي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أبا جهل -لعنه الله-

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p257/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p257/r13.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p257/r13.claim: Qatada says this taunt was revealed concerning Abu Jahl.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p257/r13.anchor: قال قتادة : نزلت في أبي جهل ، وفيه أربعة أوجه :

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p257/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p257/r14.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p257/r14.claim: Qatada says the taunt means the man is neither mighty nor noble, refuting Abu Jahl's boast that he was strongest alive.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p257/r14.anchor: أحدها : معناه أنك لست بعزيز ولا كريم , لأنه قال توعدني محمد , والله إني لأعز من مشى حبليها

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p257/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p257/r15.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p257/r15.claim: Qatada also reads it as mighty and noble in the man's own estimation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p257/r15.anchor: الثاني : أنك أنت العزيز الكريم عند نفسك , قاله قتادة أيضا .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p257/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p257/r16.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p257/r16.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says the words are sarcastic, intended to humiliate.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p257/r16.anchor: الثالث : أنه قيل له ذلك استهزاء على جهة الإهانة , قاله سعيد بن جبير .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p257/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p257/r17.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p257/r17.claim: Ibn Isa reads the taunt as mighty among his people and noble to his family.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p257/r17.anchor: الرابع : أنك أنت العزيز في قومك , الكريم على أهلك حكاه ابن عيسى .

MUQATIL:44:44-50/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:44:44-50/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:44:44-50/r9.claim: The keeper's command to taste the torment mocks and humiliates Abu Jahl.
MUQATIL:44:44-50/r9.anchor: العذاب أيها المتعزز المتكرم، يوبخه ويصغره بذلك

MUQATIL:44:44-50/r10.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:44:44-50/r10.speaker: author
MUQATIL:44:44-50/r10.claim: Aziz means impregnable, while karim here means self-honoring or conceited.
MUQATIL:44:44-50/r10.anchor: { أنت العزيز } ، يعنى المنيع، { الكريم } [آية: 49] يعنى المتكرم

MUQATIL:44:44-50/r11.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:44:44-50/r11.speaker: author
MUQATIL:44:44-50/r11.claim: Abu Jahl used to boast in worldly life that he was the mightiest and noblest of Quraysh; the keeper taunts him with that claim in Hell.
MUQATIL:44:44-50/r11.anchor: فكان أبو جهل يقول فى الدنيا: أنا أعز قريش وأكرمها، فلما ذاق شدة العذاب فى الآخرة، قال له الملك

NASAFI-FULL:v4p127#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p127#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p127#6/r1.claim: Calling the punished man mighty and noble is sarcasm and mockery; in context, inna is explained causally as “because.”
NASAFI-FULL:v4p127#6/r1.anchor: على سبيل الهزؤ والهكم انك اى لانك على

QURTUBI-FULL:44:49-50/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:44:49-50/r1.speaker: العوام، الحسن عن علي، الكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:44:49-50/r1.claim: The common readers agree on kasra in inna; al-Ḥasan reports from ʿAlī a reading with fatḥa, which al-Kisāʾī also read.
QURTUBI-FULL:44:49-50/r1.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري: أجمعت العوام على كسر «إن». وروي عن الحسن عن علي رحمه الله «ذق أنك» بفتح «أن»

QURTUBI-FULL:44:49-50/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:44:49-50/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:44:49-50/r2.claim: With kasra one pauses after “taste”; with fatḥa one does not pause, since the sense is “taste because you are the mighty and noble one.”
QURTUBI-FULL:44:49-50/r2.anchor: فمن كسر «إن» وقف على «ذق». ومن فتحها لم يقف على «ذق» لأن المعنى ذق لأنك

QURTUBI-FULL:44:49-50/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:44:49-50/r3.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:44:49-50/r3.claim: Qatāda says it concerns Abū Jahl, who had claimed that no one in the region was more powerful or honored than he; the verse taunts him with his own boast.
QURTUBI-FULL:44:49-50/r3.anchor: قال قتادة: نزلت في أبي جهل وكان قد قال: ما فيها أعز مني ولا أكرم

QURTUBI-FULL:44:49-50/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:44:49-50/r4.speaker: النبي ﷺ
QURTUBI-FULL:44:49-50/r4.claim: ʿIkrima recounts the Prophet warning Abū Jahl that God ordered him to say “woe to you”; Abū Jahl boasted of his power and honor, was killed and humiliated at Badr, and the verse was revealed.
QURTUBI-FULL:44:49-50/r4.anchor:
وقال عكرمة:
" التقى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأبو جهل

QURTUBI-FULL:44:49-50/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:44:49-50/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:44:49-50/r5.claim: The angel says this mockingly, according to Abū Jahl’s own claim that he was the mightiest and most honored in the valley.
QURTUBI-FULL:44:49-50/r5.anchor: أي يقول له الملك: ذق إنك أنت العزيز الكريم بزعمك

QURTUBI-FULL:44:49-50/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:44:49-50/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:44:49-50/r6.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reads the line as scorn, rebuke, mockery, insult, and degradation: it means “you are the lowly, humiliated one.”

QURTUBI-FULL:44:49-50/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:44:49-50/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:44:49-50/r7.claim: The taunt is compared with the people of Shuʿayb calling him “the forbearing, right-minded one,” which one interpretation takes to mean foolish and ignorant.
QURTUBI-FULL:44:49-50/r7.anchor: وهو كما قال قوم شعيب لشعيب: إنك لأنت الحليم الرشيد
